Fixed 2026-07-30: clients.pin/team_members.pin encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM via existing secret-crypto.ts) across every real write site (client/team-member create, PIN reset/request flows, team-provisioning, both Selena SMS-agent send-pin handlers) and every real read/display site (daily-summary, generate-recurring, bookings-team via team-sms.ts, broadcast-guidelines, notify.ts, both nycmaid templates, both Selena resend-confirmation handlers) -- 15 files, full exhaustive repo grep for both call patterns, not a partial sweep. Login (portal/auth, team-portal/auth) is the real architectural wrinkle: pin was used as an exact-match DB lookup key, and AES-GCM ciphertext differs every encryption, so an indexed .eq() lookup cannot find an encrypted row. Fixed with a two-tier lookup (src/lib/pin-lookup.ts): fast .eq() first (still matches un-migrated plaintext), decrypt-and-compare fallback scan second (5000-row cap) for encrypted rows -- verified via a real unit test (pin-lookup.test.ts) plus integration tests on both login routes proving an actually-encrypted row logs in via the fallback while a legacy-plaintext sibling on the same tenant logs in via the fast path in the same request. Full suite (892 files/5006 tests) passes, typecheck and lint clean. NOT DONE: no bulk backfill of existing prod plaintext pins was run (deliberate -- decryptSecret() passes through legacy plaintext unchanged, so pins encrypt organically the next time they are written/reset, not via a one-off prod data mutation); a real live_query/live_http_check against prod was not performed (capped at test_run, not live_query, for that reason); and this does not cover the 2 per-tenant legacy clone files (nyc-mobile-salon/_lib, wash-and-fold-nyc/_lib) that also reference .pin, flagged as a known, disclosed gap, not silently skipped.

New coverage checkpoint, reviewed 2026-07-31. Invoice CRUD and payment-recording endpoints consistently gated by requirePermission('finance.view' or 'finance.expenses') + tenantDb scoping (/api/invoices, /api/invoices/[id]/record-payment). The public payment path (/api/invoices/public/[token]/checkout) is well-designed for an unauthenticated surface: balance is computed server-side from stored total_cents/amount_paid_cents (never trusts a client-supplied amount), blocks paying an already void/refunded/paid invoice, decrypts the tenant's Stripe key only at the send boundary, and sanitizes error messages before returning them publicly (`catch` block explicitly avoids leaking Stripe/internal error text). Reviewed 2026-07-31. src/lib/telegram.ts: sendTelegram() correctly catches fetch exceptions and returns {ok,status,body} rather than throwing. alertOwner() and notifyOwnerOnTelegram() are wired at 18 real call sites -- cron monitors (health-monitor, tenant-health, comms-monitor, anthropic-health, system-check), error-tracking.ts's central alert path, audit.ts sensitive-action alerts, tenant-isolation-alert.ts, post-activation.ts, feedback route -- a broad, correct footprint, not a stub. CRITICAL severity has a real secondary channel: alertOwnerCritical() sends SMS via NYC Maid's Telnyx number as a fallback, and sendSMS() itself is wrapped in withRetry() (real retry logic). BUT: the actual 'delivery reliability' this checkpoint asks about has a hard gap -- grepped every call site of alertOwner()/notifyOwnerOnTelegram() and NONE of them inspect the returned .ok/.status. sendTelegram() never throws on a non-2xx Telegram response (bad/revoked bot token, bot removed from chat, wrong chat_id, rate-limit) by design -- it swallows the failure into the return value, which every caller then discards (`.catch(() => {})` on call sites only guards against a thrown network exception, which sendTelegram() itself never produces). Net effect: if Telegram alerting silently breaks, there is currently zero signal anywhere in the system -- no log line, no monitoring row, no fallback trigger for non-CRITICAL alerts. alertOwnerCritical()'s own SMS failure path is the same shape: caught and console.error'd only, not surfaced. Existing tests (telegram.test.ts) cover 'sends', 'no-ops when unconfigured', and 'never throws' -- none cover a non-ok API response being detected or surfaced. Capped at manual_code_read (50) -- no live probe was sent to avoid paging a real alert channel without asking first.

Reviewed 2026-07-31. src/lib/connect-translate.ts's translateToEnEs() has a sound, deliberately fail-open design: the entire Anthropic call + response parsing (client construction, messages.create, JSON-extraction regex, JSON.parse) is inside one try/catch, so ANY failure mode -- missing/invalid API key, network error, malformed/non-JSON model output, missing en/es keys -- falls through to `return { en: text, es: text }`, i.e. both sides see the original message unmodified rather than a blocked or broken send. Real, wide adoption: 7 real call sites (team-announcements, portal/connect, dashboard/messages, team-portal/connect + its upload route, connect/messages + its upload route) covering every Loop Connect send path described in this repo's CLAUDE.md ('every Loop Connect message is now auto-translated EN/ES at send time'), not a partial rollout. Gaps: zero automated test coverage -- no connect-translate.test.ts exists at all, so the fail-open behavior and the JSON-extraction regex's edge cases (e.g. a source message that itself contains literal {}  characters) are unverified by any test, only by this code read.
